requirements.statement: The objective of three-way matching must survive the redesign in some form; the matching function may be retained, restructured, merged or absorbed, but not eliminated.
Whatever carries the matching function must still consume PO data and GRN data.
Invoice approval must survive in some form.
Approval must occur before payment execution.
GL posting must survive; invoices cannot bypass the ledger.
The approval function and the posting function must not be performed by the same actor.
AP reconciliation must survive the redesign.
Payment execution must survive in some form.

source.document_reference: APQC PCF Cross-Industry v8.0 (Feb 2026), 9.6.1 Process accounts payable (10756); step decomposition per PhD encoding spec v1.0 with HighRadius/Conduent/AFP/Trintech practitioner documentation.

steps.description: Vendor invoices arrive through multiple channels and are logged as invoice records carrying header metadata, establishing the population of invoices entering the process.
inputs: Vendor invoice (email PDF, EDI, supplier portal or paper)
steps.name: Invoice receipt and intake

steps.description: Invoice content is extracted from the raw file and validated into a structured record covering vendor ID, invoice number, dates, amounts, currency, line items, tax and PO reference.
steps.name: Data extraction and validation

steps.description: The validated invoice is matched against purchase order and goods receipt data, yielding a clean match, a match within tolerance, or an exception.
steps.name: Purchase order matching

steps.description: Invoices flagged as exceptions are investigated against variance detail and source documents, and resolved as approved, rejected or held, with the resolution evidenced.
steps.name: Exception handling and resolution

steps.description: Matched invoices are routed through the approval hierarchy according to the approval matrix and authorised for posting.
steps.name: Approval routing and authorisation

steps.description: The approved invoice is coded to the chart of accounts, cost centres and project codes, then posted to the general ledger and the accounts payable subledger.
steps.name: GL coding and posting

steps.description: Posted invoices are scheduled against payment terms, vendor bank details and the cash position; a payment file is generated, transmitted and confirmed.
steps.name: Payment scheduling and execution

steps.description: Bank confirmations, the AP subledger and vendor statements are reconciled, and the period-end accounts payable balance is confirmed.
steps.name: Reconciliation and period close
